3-in-1 vector vaccine expands disease-protection options for chickens, backed by Zoetis’ comprehensive vaccine portfolio and specialized expertise 

  • What it protects against: Poulvac® Procerta® HVT-ND-ILT is designed to protect chickens against Marek’s disease (MD), Newcastle disease (ND) and infectious laryngotracheitis (ILT). 1
  • Why it matters: The USDA license adds a new option for veterinarians and poultry producers to consider when developing flock-health programs.

PARSIPPANY, N.J.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Zoetis Inc. (NYSE: ZTS) today announced that the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) has licensed Poulvac® Procerta® HVT-ND-ILT, a vector vaccine for chickens. The license marks an important milestone in Zoetis’ continued investment and industry leadership in poultry health, disease protection, and innovation. Poulvac Procerta HVT-ND-ILT brings three disease targets together in one vaccine and expands the tools available to poultry veterinarians and producers as they develop vaccination programs.

“The USDA license is an important achievement for our poultry business and reflects Zoetis’ commitment to advancing practical solutions for customers,” said Abhay Nayak, Executive Vice President and President, U.S. Commercial Operations at Zoetis. “Poulvac Procerta HVT-ND-ILT adds a new option to our portfolio, giving veterinarians and producers more flexibility to tailor their vaccination strategies. Our team looks forward to working with customers as they consider how it may support their flock-health programs.”

3-in-1 protection veterinarians can count on

ILT remains an economically significant respiratory disease, with outbreaks capable of causing significant losses in flocks. 2 Poulvac Procerta HVT-ND-ILT is designed to provide early, long-lasting protection against Marek’s disease (MD), Newcastle disease (ND) and infectious laryngotracheitis (ILT). 1 It is labeled for administration to healthy one-day-old chickens or 18- to 19-day-old embryonated chicken eggs.

More flexibility in vaccination programs

Zoetis’ poultry vaccine portfolio gives veterinarians options to build vaccination programs around flock needs and disease challenges. Poulvac Procerta HVT-ND-ILT can be included in seasonal or rotational ILT programs that also use modified-live vaccines. It complements other Poulvac® hatchery and immune-complex vaccines designed to address additional disease challenges, including infectious bursal disease, infectious bronchitis, Salmonella and E. coli.

Support beyond the vaccine

Zoetis poultry specialists support customers by helping plan and implement targeted vaccination programs that optimize bird health and well-being. Tailored support can include technical guidance, diagnostic testing and analysis, hatchery services and team training, as well as vaccine audits and flock-health assessments.

About Zoetis

Zoetis is the world’s leading animal health company, driven by a singular purpose: to nurture our world and humankind by advancing care for animals. With a legacy of nearly 75 years, Zoetis continues to pioneer ways to predict, prevent, detect, and treat animal illness, supporting veterinarians, livestock producers, and pet owners in over 100 countries. We integrate deep scientific expertise, data-driven R&D, advanced manufacturing, and commercial excellence to deliver meaningful innovation across medicines, vaccines, diagnostics, biopharmaceuticals, and digital solutions. Guided by our vision to be the most trusted and valued animal health company, Zoetis is committed to setting new standards for the future of animal care through innovation, customer obsession, and purpose-driven colleagues. Key Terms

vector vaccinetechnical
A vaccine that uses a harmless virus (a viral vector) as a delivery vehicle to carry genetic instructions for a disease-causing protein (antigen) into human cells; those cells then produce the antigen so the immune system learns to recognize it. Vectors can be engineered so they cannot replicate, or left replication‑competent in a controlled way, and the body's immune response may target both the antigen and the vector itself, which can affect repeat dosing or vaccine effectiveness.
modified-live vaccinesmedical
Vaccines that use live microorganisms (viruses or bacteria) that have been weakened or genetically altered so they can replicate only to a limited degree in the body and no longer cause the disease they would in an unvaccinated person. Because the modified organism can briefly reproduce, these vaccines tend to produce a strong, broad immune response similar to natural infection; however, they are not the same as inactivated (killed) or subunit vaccines and are generally unsuitable for people with severely weakened immune systems or other specific medical contraindications.

Partnership combines WebMD ONE, a trusted engagement platform, with Dario's comprehensive AI-powered multi-condition platform and clinical care solutions to help employers, health plans and health systems translate engagement into measurable health outcomes and in-year healthcare cost savings

Revenue contribution to Dario to begin in 2027

NEW YORK, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- DarioHealth Corp. (NASDAQ: DRIO), a leading AI-powered healthcare technology company transforming the management of chronic conditions, today announced a strategic partnership with WebMD Health Services, one of the industry's leading well-being and population health organizations serving more than 3,500 employers, health plans, health systems and public sector organizations.  Dario expects the partnership to begin contributing annual recurring revenue ("ARR") in 2027, including via distribution through the administrative services organization ("ASO") of a leading integrated healthcare system serving a broad network of hospitals and healthcare services.

The partnership brings Dario's comprehensive multi-condition whole-person care platform to the WebMD ecosystem, combining WebMD's trusted risk identification, engagement and behavior change capabilities with Dario's clinically validated care programs, provider backed care, and DarioIQ, its AI-driven intelligence engine that uses proprietary longitudinal health data to personalize member engagement and interventions. These capabilities are designed to help organizations convert member engagement into meaningful clinical outcomes while addressing multiple health needs through a single integrated platform.

Through the partnership, WebMD Health Services will offer Dario's full suite of integrated solutions, including cardiometabolic care, behavioral health, musculoskeletal care with posture management, obstructive sleep apnea ("OSA"), women's health, including perimenopause and menopause support, GLP-1 support programs and access-to-care capabilities through Dario's provider network.

"This partnership with WebMD brings together the key growth drivers we have been building across Dario," said Erez Raphael, Chief Executive Officer of Dario. "WebMD Health Services is a trusted partner that gives us the opportunity to introduce our solutions to employers and health plans across its client base, which represents millions of lives. As clients choose to add Dario, our multi-condition platform creates the opportunity to deliver multiple solutions through each new customer relationship. DarioIQ enables us to personalize engagement at scale, and our provider-backed care capabilities extend our role further into the care journey. Together, these capabilities create a powerful model for expanding both our reach and revenue as we partner with the leading name in health and well-being."

The collaboration enables organizations already leveraging WebMD Health Services to seamlessly connect members from WebMD ONE into personalized clinical interventions across multiple chronic conditions, creating a more unified approach to whole-person health while reducing the complexity of managing multiple point solutions and delivering improving return on investment ("ROI") and healthcare cost savings. A recent independent analysis of published peer-reviewed studies confirmed that Dario's platform has the potential to reduce total healthcare costs for payers by up to 10% in-year.  

"We're committed to delivering outcomes-based solutions that help our clients reduce risk and manage costs, while improving the health and well-being of their populations," said John Harrison, President and General Manager of WebMD Health Services. "Our partnership with Dario builds on the cost containment solutions already available through WebMD ONE and gives organizations another way to address risk where it matters most. By connecting engagement with personalized clinical support at a higher level of clinical acuity, clients can achieve measurable outcomes and more effective cost management across a broad range of health needs."

The partnership represents another milestone in Dario's strategy of delivering its AI-powered, whole-person care platform through premier ecosystem partners, making comprehensive digital health more accessible while helping organizations improve outcomes, enhance member experiences and maximize the value of their well-being and health investments.

data.title: Biohaven's Novel FGFR3-Directed ADC with Proprietary TopoIx Payload, BHV-1530, Shows Clinical Activity and Confirmed Responses in FGFR3-Altered Urothelial and Head and Neck Cancers, Oral Presentation at ENA 2026 | BHVN Stock News
data.description:

Phase 1 data presented in an oral plenary session at the 38th EORTC-NCI-AACR Symposium on Molecular Targets and Cancer Therapeutics (ENA 2026) in Barcelona, Spain, showed deep and durable responses in patients with FGFR3-altered urothelial cancer (UC) and head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC). As of the data cutoff in the ongoing study, 6 of 10 evaluable patients with FGFR3 activating alterations treated at doses of ≥3.3 mg/kg had responded, including 3 of 5 with UC and 3 of 3 with HPV-positive HNSCC.

  • Responders to BHV-1530 in UC included patients who failed prior enfortumab vedotin plus pembrolizumab (EV+P) and oral FGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors. All responders remained on treatment at data cutoff, some beyond 6 months.

  • BHV-1530 was well tolerated with no FGFR class toxicities: no DLTs, treatment-related SAEs or deaths, and no ILD; no hyperphosphatemia, nail dystrophy or central serous retinopathy.

  • Biohaven completed FDA Type C meeting in 4Q 2026 and plans to initiate a pivotal study evaluating BHV-1530 in FGFR3-altered tumors, starting with UC, expected to begin as early as 1H 2027 to support potential accelerated approval.

BARCELONA, Spain and NEW HAVEN, Conn., Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Biohaven Ltd. (NYSE: BHVN) ("Biohaven"), a global clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on the discovery, development and commercialization of life-changing therapies to treat a broad range of rare and common diseases, today announced clinical data from the ongoing Phase 1 study of BHV-1530, its first in class potential FGFR3-directed antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) with a novel topoisomerase I (TopoIx) payload. The data were presented today by Gerald S. Falchook, M.D., Director of Sarah Cannon Research Institute at HCA HealthONE, in an oral presentation during Plenary Session 3 at the 38th EORTC-NCI-AACR Symposium on Molecular Targets and Cancer Therapeutics (ENA 2026) in Barcelona, Spain. As of the October 19, 2026 data cutoff, 30 patients had received BHV-1530 monotherapy every three weeks (Q3W) at doses from 1.0 to 12.0 mg/kg, and dose escalation is ongoing. Patients had received a median of two prior lines of therapy for advanced disease, and all patients with UC had progressed on EV+P.

Among 10 efficacy-evaluable patients with activating FGFR3 alterations, treated with BHV-1530 at doses of 3.3 mg/kg or higher, 9/10 had a tumor reduction and 6 achieved a partial response (PR; confirmed or unconfirmed, by investigator assessment per RECIST v1.1; Figure 1). Responses were observed in tumors with FGFR3 mutations and fusions, including in 3 of 5 patients with UC and all 3 patients with HPV-positive HNSCC. All responders remained on treatment as of the data cutoff, some for more than 6 months.

Gerald S. Falchook, M.D. commented, "Many patients in this study had progressed on multiple prior therapies, including enfortumab vedotin plus pembrolizumab and FGFR inhibitors in urothelial cancer, so seeing durable responses is very encouraging." Dr. Falchook added, "We also saw deep responses in HPV-positive head and neck cancer, where options after immunotherapy are limited. Importantly, BHV-1530 has been well tolerated, with no dose-limiting toxicities and none of the hyperphosphatemia, nail or retinal toxicities that often restrict FGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor therapy."

In UC, where all patients had progressed on prior EV+P, partial responses occurred in 3 of 5 patients with FGFR3-altered tumors, including a patient who had also received a prior FGFR inhibitor. Tumor reductions were also observed in the 2 patients with FGFR3 wild-type tumors, including one partial response pending confirmation (Figure 2).

Dr. Falchook presented the clinical case of a patient with HPV-positive metastatic HNSCC and an FGFR3 S249C mutation, who had received four prior lines of therapy including chemoradiation, a platinum doublet and immunotherapy. This patient achieved a confirmed partial response, with a 67% reduction in target lesions at Week 6 that deepened to 86% by Week 24, (Figure 3) and remains on therapy beyond 6 months with no treatment-related adverse events. This case illustrates the speed and depth of response in a highly refractory patient who failed prior standard of care.

BHV-1530 was well tolerated across all dose levels in 30 patients, with no dose-limiting toxicities, treatment-related serious adverse events or treatment-related deaths. The most common adverse events, nausea (43%) and fatigue (37%), were all Grade 1 or 2. Hematological toxicity was mostly low grade and manageable. None of the toxicities that commonly limit FGFR inhibitor therapy (hyperphosphatemia, nail dystrophy or central serous retinopathy) were observed, and no interstitial lung disease (ILD) was reported. Pharmacokinetic data showed that BHV-1530 is highly stable in circulation, with free payload exposure below 1% of ADC exposure, and a half-life of 7 to 14 days that supports Q3W dosing.

Nushmia Khokhar, M.D., Chief Medical Officer of Oncology at Biohaven stated, "Unlike FGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors, which block kinase signaling inside the cell, BHV-1530 is an ADC designed to bind FGFR3 on the tumor cell surface, be internalized and release a potent topoisomerase I payload, independent of kinase-domain resistance mutations."

Dr. Khokhar added, "Following a recent Type C meeting with the FDA, we are excited to advance BHV-1530 into a pivotal study in FGFR3-altered tumors, beginning with urothelial cancer, as early as the first half of 2027, with the goal of supporting a potential accelerated approval."

FGFR3 is frequently altered or overexpressed in UC. Activating mutations or fusions, together with overexpression of the wild-type receptor, are found in about half of metastatic UC and in 70% to 80% of non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer, and are also seen in head and neck, lung and other solid tumors (Figure 4). Enfortumab vedotin plus pembrolizumab is now the first-line standard of care for advanced UC, but many patients eventually progress and options after progression remain limited. The only FDA-approved FGFR-targeted therapy for advanced UC is an oral pan-FGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI), indicated only for previously treated patients whose tumors carry a susceptible FGFR3 alteration, which leaves patients whose tumors overexpress wild-type FGFR3 without a targeted option. Pan-FGFR TKIs also inhibit FGFR1, FGFR2 and FGFR4, and their labeled class effects include hyperphosphatemia, nail disorders, stomatitis and retinopathy, which often require dose interruptions or reductions. Resistance can also emerge through mutations in the kinase domain where these drugs bind. BHV-1530 is designed to bind FGFR3 on the tumor cell surface rather than inhibit its kinase, and is being studied in patients with and without FGFR3 alterations.

BHV-1530 takes a different approach to FGFR3 than approved pan-FGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors, which block kinase signaling across the FGFR family (Figure 5). The investigational antibody-drug conjugate is designed to bind selectively to FGFR3 on the tumor cell surface and deliver its TopoIx payload inside the cell, with no detectable binding to FGFR1, FGFR2 or FGFR4 in preclinical studies.

About Study BHV1530-101

BHV1530-101 (NCT06874335) is a Phase 1, first-in-human, multicenter study of BHV-1530 as monotherapy and in combination with an anti-PD-1 antibody in adults with advanced solid tumors. Patients with UC, HNSCC or non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) were enrolled irrespective of FGFR3 alteration status, without a minimum FGFR3 expression threshold. Patients with other solid tumors were eligible if their tumors harbored an activating FGFR3 alteration.

About BHV-1530

BHV-1530 is an antibody-drug conjugate directed against FGFR3, a validated but underexploited target in urothelial cancer and other FGFR3-driven cancers and is a first-in-class potential FGFR3-directed ADC incorporating Biohaven's proprietary TopoIx payload. Unlike approved FGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors, which are restricted to genomically selected patients and constrained by class-related toxicities, BHV-1530 is designed to target FGFR3 with the potential to address both FGFR3-altered and wild-type overexpressing tumors. BHV-1530 is being studied in an ongoing Phase 1 dose-escalation trial in unselected patients with advanced urothelial cancer, head and neck squamous cell carcinoma, and non-small cell lung cancer who have failed standard-of-care therapy, as well as other tumor types harboring FGFR3 genomic alterations. Biohaven has initiated combination cohorts evaluating BHV-1530 with anti-PD-1 therapy, including the combination with LIBTAYO® (cemiplimab) which is now enrolling.

NEW YORK--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Warner Music Group Corp. today announced its fourth-quarter and full-year financial results for the periods ended September 30, 2026.

“Our Q4 and full-year results demonstrate the success of a multi-year, transformational strategy that sets a new bar for WMG,” said Robert Kyncl, CEO, Warner Music Group. “Our creative prowess paired with a disciplined, return-focused capital allocation approach, and tech-enabled capabilities, positions us to drive sustainable, long-term value for our artists, songwriters, and shareholders in fiscal 2027 and beyond.”

“With revenue reaching an all-time high, led by double-digit subscription streaming growth and margin expansion ahead of our expectation, we delivered against our financial goals in 2026,” said Lou Dickler, Acting CFO. “Supported by contractual per-subscriber minimum increases, sustained global market share gains, and rigorous cost discipline, we enter fiscal 2027 with substantial momentum and a clear roadmap for continued growth.”

Fourth-Quarter Results

Revenue was up 7.1% (or 7.5% in constant currency). Consistent with prior quarters, Recorded Music revenue growth was unfavorably impacted by the termination of the distribution agreement with BMG (the “BMG Termination”), which resulted in $7 million less Recorded Music digital revenue compared to the prior-year quarter. Excluding the BMG Termination, total revenue was up 7.5% (or 7.9% in constant currency).

Digital revenue increased 13.2% (or 13.1% in constant currency) and streaming revenue increased 13.7% (or 13.5% in constant currency). Recorded Music streaming revenue increased 13.4% (or 13.2% in constant currency); however, adjusted for the $7 million impact of the BMG Termination, Recorded Music streaming revenue was up 14.3% (or 14.0% in constant currency) driven by continued market growth, including upside from price and wholesale rate increases, as well as market share gains. Music Publishing streaming revenue increased 15.1% (the same in constant currency). Revenue increases in the quarter were also driven by growth in Recorded Music physical and licensing revenue, partially offset by lower Recorded Music artist services and expanded-rights revenue and Music Publishing performance and mechanical revenue. Music Publishing synchronization revenue remained constant.

Operating income increased by $177 million to $320 million in the quarter from $143 million in the prior-year quarter, primarily due to revenue mix and a $107 million decrease in restructuring and non-cash impairment charges compared to the prior-year quarter, and a $7 million decrease in amortization expense, as well as factors affecting Adjusted OIBDA discussed below, partially offset by a $21 million increase in non-cash stock-based compensation costs due to accelerated expense recognition associated with executive transition and involuntary terminations coupled with higher vesting expense of outstanding awards.

Adjusted OIBDA increased 17.8% from $405 million to $477 million (or 17.2% in constant currency) and Adjusted OIBDA margin increased 2.1 percentage points to 23.8% from 21.7% (or 1.9 percentage points from 21.9% in constant currency), primarily driven by strong operating performance, revenue mix and savings from the Company’s restructuring plans, a portion of which has been reinvested into the Company’s business.

Net income increased by $70 million to $179 million from $109 million in the prior-year quarter. The increase was primarily due to the factors affecting operating income described above, and the impact of exchange rates on the Company’s Euro-denominated debt resulting in a gain of $7 million compared to a loss of $1 million in the prior-year quarter, partially offset by a loss of $1 million on intercompany loans compared to a gain of $13 million in the prior-year quarter. The increase was also partially offset by a tax expense of $98 million in the quarter compared to a benefit of $3 million in the prior-year quarter driven by higher pre-tax income and tax expense recognized in connection with a change in our indefinite reinvestment assertion.

Basic and Diluted earnings per share were $0.34 for both the Class A and Class B shareholders due to net income attributable to the Company in the quarter of $179 million.

As of September 30, 2026, the Company reported a cash balance of $589 million, total debt of $4.704 billion and net debt (defined as total debt, net of deferred financing costs, premiums and discounts, minus cash and equivalents) of $4.115 billion, compared to $3.833 billion at the end of the prior year. Total debt as of September 30, 2026 includes $303 million of subsidiary debt acquired in the Company’s acquisition of Tempo Music Holdings, LLC (“Tempo Music”) and $363 million in loans outstanding under the Beethoven JV. The debt is secured only by certain music rights owned by Tempo Music and the Beethoven JV, respectively, and is nonrecourse to the Company and its subsidiaries, other than Tempo Music and the Beethoven JV, respectively.

Cash provided by operating activities decreased 32% to $158 million from $231 million in the prior-year quarter. The decrease was largely the result of timing of working capital, including the timing of payments related to the Company’s restructuring plans and contractual digital advances, partially offset by strong operating performance. Capital expenditures decreased to $25 million, from $28 million in the prior-year quarter. Free Cash Flow, as defined below, decreased $70 million to $133 million from $203 million in the prior-year quarter.

Full-Year Results

Total revenue increased 10.9% (or 8.9% in constant currency). As previously disclosed, Recorded Music revenue growth was impacted by a $12 million digital revenue settlement in the year and $4 million for performance obligations satisfied in previous periods in the prior year (the “DSP True-Up and Settlement Payments”) as well as $16 million in digital revenue from the settlement of certain infringement cases in the prior year (the “Copyright Settlement”). In addition, revenue growth was unfavorably impacted by the BMG Termination, which resulted in a $29 million decrease in Recorded Music digital revenue compared to the prior year. Music Publishing revenue was impacted by $17 million of revenue in the prior year recognized in connection with the historical matched royalties that were processed to date by the Mechanical Licensing Collective (the “MLC Historical Matched Royalties”). Adjusted for these items, total revenue was up 11.8% (or 9.8% in constant currency).

Digital revenue increased 12.5% (or 10.4% in constant currency) and streaming revenue increased 13.4% (or 11.2% in constant currency). Recorded Music streaming revenue increased 13.5% (or 11.1% in constant currency). Adjusted for the impact of the DSP True-Up and Settlement Payments of $12 million in the current year and $4 million in the prior year, and the impact of the BMG Termination of $29 million in the prior year, Recorded Music streaming revenue increased 14.2% (or 11.8% in constant currency) driven by continued market growth, including upside from price and wholesale rate increases, as well as market share gains. Music Publishing streaming revenue increased 13.0% (or 11.5% in constant currency). Adjusted for the $17 million impact of the MLC Historical Matched Royalties, Music Publishing streaming revenue increased 15.5% (or 13.9% in constant currency). Revenue increases in the year were also driven by growth in Recorded Music artist services and expanded-rights, physical and licensing revenue and Music Publishing performance, synchronization and mechanical revenue.

Operating income increased by $483 million to $1,177 million from $694 million in the prior year. The increase in operating income was primarily due to revenue mix, savings from the Company’s strategic restructuring plans, a portion of which has been reinvested in the Company’s business, and factors that led to the increase in Adjusted OIBDA discussed below, partially offset by a $25 million increase in amortization expense and a $9 million increase in depreciation expense.

Adjusted OIBDA increased 22.7% to $1,770 million from $1,443 million (or 19.4% in constant currency). Adjusted OIBDA margin increased 2.3 percentage points to 23.8% from 21.5% in the prior year (or 2.1 percentage points from 21.7% in constant currency). The increases in Adjusted OIBDA and Adjusted OIBDA margin include the impact of the DSP True-Up and Settlement Payments of $7 million in the current year and $3 million in the prior year, and the impact of the Copyright Settlement of $9 million, the MLC Historical Matched Royalties of $4 million and the BMG Termination of $2 million in the prior year. Excluding the impact of these items, Adjusted OIBDA increased 23.7% (or 20.4% in constant currency) and Adjusted OIBDA margin increased 2.2 percentage points to 23.7% from 21.5% in the prior year (or 2.1 percentage points from 21.6% in constant currency), primarily due to revenue mix and cost savings from the Company’s restructuring plans, a portion of which has been reinvested in the Company’s business, partially offset by unfavorable movements in foreign currency exchange rates of approximately $8 million.

Net income increased by $365 million to $735 million from $370 million in the prior year. The increase in net income was primarily due to the factors described above, partially offset by higher income tax expense of $189 million, driven by higher pre-tax income and tax expense recognized in connection with a change in our indefinite reinvestment assertion in the current year as compared to the tax benefit recognized in the prior year from impairment of EMP.

Basic earnings per share was $1.41 for Class A shareholders and $1.40 for Class B shareholders due to net income attributable to the Company in the year of $735 million. Diluted earnings per share was $1.39 for Class A shareholders and $1.40 for Class B shareholders.

Cash provided by operating activities increased 28% to $866 million from $678 million in the prior year. The change was largely a result of strong operating performance, partially offset by the timing of working capital, including payments related to the Company’s restructuring plans and contractual digital advances. Operating cash flow conversion was 49% of Adjusted OIBDA. Capital expenditures decreased 28% to $100 million from $139 million in the prior year. Free Cash Flow, as defined below, increased $227 million to $766 million from $539 million in the prior year.

Fourth-Quarter Results

Music Publishing revenue increased 7.7% (or 7.4% in constant currency) driven by higher digital revenue, partially offset by lower performance and mechanical revenue. Digital revenue increased 14.9% (the same in constant currency) and streaming revenue increased 15.1% (the same in constant currency), which reflects continued market growth and the impact of deal renewals. Performance revenue decreased 6.6% (the same in constant currency) primarily due to the timing of payments from collection societies. Synchronization revenue remained constant compared to the prior-year quarter (or decreased 1.8% in constant currency). Mechanical revenue decreased 5.9% (the same in constant currency).

Music Publishing operating income increased to $65 million from $57 million in the prior-year quarter and operating margin increased 1.0 percentage point to 17.9% from 16.9% in the prior-year quarter. The increase in operating income and operating income margin were primarily driven by the same factors affecting Adjusted OIBDA discussed below, partially offset by a $2 million increase in amortization expense.

Adjusted OIBDA increased 15.5% to $112 million from $97 million (or 14.3% in constant currency) and Adjusted OIBDA margin increased 2.1 percentage points to 30.9% from 28.8% in the prior-year quarter (or 1.9 percentage points from 29.0% in constant currency). The increases in Adjusted OIBDA and Adjusted OIBDA margin were primarily driven by revenue growth.

Full-Year Results

Music Publishing revenue increased 11.4% (or 9.3% in constant currency) driven by growth in digital, performance, synchronization, and mechanical revenue. Excluding the impact of the MLC Historical Matched Royalties, Music Publishing revenue increased 12.9% (or 10.7% in constant currency). Digital revenue increased 13.1% (or 11.6% in constant currency) driven by growth in streaming revenue of 13.0% (or 11.5% in constant currency). Adjusted for the impact of the MLC Historical Matched Royalties, streaming revenue increased 15.5% (or 13.9% in constant currency) reflecting continued market growth and the impact of deal renewals. Performance revenue increased 4.4% (or 1.3% in constant currency) primarily due to the favorable impact of foreign currency exchange rates. Synchronization revenue increased 14.2% (or 11.4% in constant currency) driven by the timing of other copyright-infringement settlements primarily in the United States, higher television and commercial licensing activity and the impact of the Company’s acquisitions, including a $3 million impact from the prior-year acquisition of Tempo. Mechanical revenue increased 11.1% (or 9.4% in constant currency) driven by the timing of distributions.

Music Publishing operating income increased to $262 million from $224 million in the prior year and operating margin increased 0.8 percentage points to 18.0% versus 17.2%, primarily driven by the same factors affecting Adjusted OIBDA discussed below and a $2 million decrease in depreciation expense, partially offset by a $17 million increase in amortization expense and an unfavorable movement in foreign currency exchange rates of approximately $1 million.

Adjusted OIBDA increased 16.3% to $420 million from $361 million (or 14.4% in constant currency) and Adjusted OIBDA margin increased 1.3 percentage points to 28.9% from 27.6% (the same in constant currency). The increases in Adjusted OIBDA and Adjusted OIBDA margin were primarily driven by strong operating performance and revenue growth, partially offset by the $4 million impact of the MLC Historical Matched Royalties in the prior year and the unfavorable movement in foreign currency exchange rates.

Supplemental Disclosures Regarding Non-GAAP Financial Measures

We evaluate our operating performance based on several factors, including the following non-GAAP financial measures:

Adjusted OIBDA and Adjusted OIBDA margin

We allocate resources and evaluate performance based on several factors, including Adjusted OIBDA. We define Adjusted OIBDA as operating income (loss) adjusted to exclude the following non-operational, discrete, or non-cash items to facilitate period-over-period comparability: (i) non-cash depreciation of tangible assets, (ii) non-cash amortization of intangible assets, (iii) non-cash stock-based compensation and other related expenses, (iv) gains or losses on divestitures, (v) expenses related to restructuring, impairment, and transformation initiatives, which include costs associated with the Company’s financial transformation initiative to design and implement new information technology and upgrade our finance infrastructure, and (vi) executive transition costs. We define Adjusted OIBDA margin as Adjusted OIBDA as a percentage of revenue. Items excluded are not viewed to contribute directly to management’s evaluation of operating results. We consider Adjusted OIBDA and Adjusted OIBDA margin to be important indicators of the operational strengths and performance of our businesses. However, a limitation of the use of Adjusted OIBDA and Adjusted OIBDA margin as performance measures is that they do not reflect the periodic costs of certain capitalized tangible and intangible assets used in generating revenues in our businesses. Accordingly, Adjusted OIBDA and Adjusted OIBDA margin should be considered in addition to, not as a substitute for, operating income (loss), operating income (loss) margin, net income (loss) attributable to Warner Music Group Corp. and other measures of financial performance reported in accordance with United States generally accepted accounting principles (“U.S. GAAP”). In addition, our definitions of Adjusted OIBDA and Adjusted OIBDA margin may differ from similarly titled measures used by other companies.

Adjusted Net Income and Adjusted EPS

We define Adjusted Net Income as net income (loss) attributable to Warner Music Group Corp. adjusted to exclude the following non-operational, discrete, or non-cash items to facilitate period-over-period comparability: (i) non-cash amortization of intangible assets, (ii) expenses related to restructuring and transformation initiatives, which include costs associated with the Company’s financial transformation initiative to design and implement new information technology and upgrade our finance infrastructure, (iii) gains or losses on divestitures, (iv) non-cash stock-based compensation, (v) loss on extinguishment of debt, (vi) executive transition costs, (vii) other (income) expenses, and (viii) certain discrete tax items. Excluding the impact of certain discrete tax items, these exclusions are then further adjusted to account for tax effects. Adjusted Net Income should be considered in addition to, not as a substitute for, net income (loss) attributable to Warner Music Group Corp. and other measures of financial performance reported in accordance with U.S. GAAP. We use Adjusted Net Income to calculate Adjusted Earnings (Loss) Per Share (“EPS”), which we define as Adjusted Net Income divided by the basic weighted-average shares outstanding for the period. Our definition of Adjusted Net Income and Adjusted EPS may differ from similarly titled measures used by other companies.

Constant Currency

Because exchange rates are an important factor in understanding period-to-period comparisons, we believe the presentation of revenue on a constant-currency basis in addition to reported revenue helps improve the ability to understand our operating results and evaluate our performance in comparison to prior periods. Constant-currency information compares results between periods as if exchange rates had remained constant period over period. We use results on a constant-currency basis as one measure to evaluate our performance. We calculate constant-currency results by applying current-year foreign currency exchange rates to prior-year results. However, a limitation of the use of the constant-currency results as a performance measure is that it does not reflect the impact of exchange rates on our revenue. These results should be considered in addition to, not as a substitute for, results reported in accordance with U.S. GAAP. Results on a constant-currency basis, as we present them, may not be comparable to similarly titled measures used by other companies and are not a measure of performance presented in accordance with U.S. GAAP.

Exceptional Gold Intercepts Across Multiple Vein Systems at the Blueberry Contact Zone

Vancouver, British Columbia--(Newsfile Corp. - November 19, 2026) - Scottie Resources Corp. (TSXV: SCOT) (OTCQB: SCTSF) (FSE: SR80) ("Scottie" or the "Company") is pleased to report additional high-grade gold intercepts from its 2026 drilling at the Blueberry Contact Zone within the Scottie Gold Mine Project. The road-accessible Scottie Gold Mine Project, which includes the 100% owned historic mine and adjacent Blueberry Contact Zone, is located 35 kilometres north of Stewart, British Columbia.

This latest batch of 2026 drill results delivers significant high-grade gold intercepts across the Blueberry, Fifi and Lemoffe vein systems reinforcing grade and continuity of the established mineralisation. This support the potential conversion of Inferred to Indicated resources, while a separate high-grade intercept below the modelled Blueberry 5 vein highlights the potential for additional mineralised structures. High-grade intercepts at Fifi and Lemoffe, including several beyond the existing PEA stope outlines, further demonstrate opportunities for resource growth and potential expansion of the PEA mine design.

The 2026 drilling program at the Scottie Gold Mine Project has concluded, with 61,578 metres ("m") drilled across 227 holes and assay results for the majority of holes still outstanding. Results from the program will inform the Company's updated Mineral Resource Estimate ("MRE") and Feasibility Study, both targeted for the first half of 2027. Figures 1-5 illustrate the reported drilling relative to the modelled vein zones.

Investors are encouraged to visit our website www.scottieresources.com to view the interactive 3D model showing the distribution of these released holes relative to modeled geology and prior drilling results.

Highlights

  • Exceptional high-grade infill results at Blueberry 3 and 4: Hole SR26-560 returned 25.5 grams per tonne (g/t) gold over 14.00 metres (m), including 17.6 g/t gold over 8.00 m at Blueberry 3 (including 29.5 g/t gold over 4.50 m) and 72.1 g/t gold over 3.00 m at Blueberry 4. Located about 20 m beyond the existing PEA stope outline, this intercept reinforces the strength of the established mineralised system while highlighting the potential to expand the mineable envelope beyond the current PEA design (Table 1, Figures 1 and 2).

  • High-grade gold intercept beyond existing vein models: Hole SR26-522 intersected 120.0 g/t gold over 1.50 m, approximately 20 m below the modelled Blueberry 5 vein, highlighting the potential for additional high-grade mineralisation beyond the currently modelled veins (Table 1, Figure 1).

  • High-grade mineralisation continues at Fifi: Hole SR26-563 intersected 10.1 g/t gold over 11.00 m, including 50.1 g/t gold over 2.00 m, in the upper portion of Fifi 1, approximately 40 m beyond the 2025 PEA stope outline. At Fifi 2, hole SR26-540 returned 5.8 g/t gold over 6.85 m, including 33.0 g/t gold over 1.00 m, approximately 30 m outboard of the existing PEA stope outline. Additional intercepts of 6.2 g/t gold over 4.00 m at Fifi 3 (SR26-563) and 8.3 g/t gold over 2.50 m at Fifi 2 (SR26-560) reinforce the potential to expand the existing resource across the Fifi vein system (Table 1, Figures 1, 3 and 4).

  • Drilling reinforces high-grade mineralisation at Lemoffe 4: Hole SR26-525 intersected 8.5 g/t gold over 3.75 m just outside the existing resource and 2025 PEA stope outline, as well as 11.7 g/t gold over 1.35 m approximately 10 m below the modelled vein. Additional results include 3.9 g/t gold over 5.90 m, including 15.2 g/t gold over 1.35 m in SR26-564, outside the existing resource blocks, while SR26-559 and SR26-565 returned 5.4 g/t gold over 4.65 m and 2.7 g/t gold over 7.00 m, respectively, within the current PEA mine design. These results reinforce grade and continuity within the established Lemoffe 4 system while highlighting potential additions beyond the existing resource and mine plan (Table 1, Figures 1 and 5).

"The results we're seeing from the Blueberry Contact Zone continue to impress, and this latest round of drilling is no exception," commented Dr. Thomas Mumford, President and CEO of Scottie Resources. "We're not only reinforcing the strength of the existing resource, but also identifying high-grade mineralisation that could meaningfully enhance the current PEA mine design. As we move toward our updated Mineral Resource Estimate and Feasibility Study, we believe these results will further augment an already compelling project."

Standards, blanks, and duplicate samples were taken at intervals and frequencies that meet or exceed industry best practices. A secure chain of custody is maintained in transporting and storing all samples. Gold is assayed using a fire assay with atomic absorption spectrometry and gravimetric finish when required (+9 g/t gold). Toronto, Ontario--(Newsfile Corp. - November 19, 2026) - Tartisan Nickel Corp. (CSE: TN) (OTCQB: TTSRF) (FSE: 8TA) ("Tartisan" or the "Company") is pleased to announce that its wholly owned subsidiary, Canadian Arrow Mines Limited, has received Early Exploration Permit PR-26-000146 for the Turtle Pond Nickel-Copper-Cobalt Project, approximately 40 kilometres south of Dryden in Northwestern Ontario. The Ontario Ministry of Energy and Mines issued the three-year permit on November 17, 2026.

Turtle Pond is located approximately 70 kilometres east of Tartisan's Kenbridge Nickel-Copper-Cobalt Project near Sioux Narrows. The two properties form part of the Company's regional critical minerals portfolio. As exploration advances, Tartisan intends to assess opportunities for future operational synergies between the projects.

Proposed Exploration Program

The proposed program comprises 14 diamond drill holes totalling approximately 2,880 metres in two phases. The first phase consists of six holes totalling approximately 1,060 metres at the Double E, Night Danger and Glatz showings. These holes are designed to twin selected historical holes, evaluate historical results and geological relationships, and provide fresh core for potential metallurgical testing.

The second phase comprises eight holes totalling approximately 1,820 metres to test electromagnetic conductors, magnetic anomalies and interpreted extensions of known mineralization. Targets are informed by ground electromagnetic and airborne geophysical surveys completed in 2024 and 2025.

Supporting work includes geological mapping, surface sampling, Beep Mat surveying and brushing of existing access trails, with surface exploration focused in part on the approximately 1.5-kilometre corridor between North Glatz and Emmons Lake. Final drill locations, sequencing and metres will be refined as field information becomes available. The proposed work remains subject to financing, contractor availability, permit conditions and any additional authorizations required.

"The Turtle Pond permit allows us to advance planning for a program that will revisit the Double E, Night Danger and Glatz showings and test additional geophysical targets," said Mark Appleby, President and CEO of Tartisan. "Turtle Pond's proximity to Kenbridge adds to its strategic interest within our Ontario portfolio. Our objective is to build a clearer understanding of its nickel-copper-cobalt potential through systematic exploration."

Nickel-copper-cobalt sulphide mineralization, with associated platinum and palladium reported at Double E, occurs in mafic and ultramafic intrusive rocks within the Wabigoon Subprovince of the Archean Superior Province. Further drilling is required to evaluate the extent and continuity of mineralization.

Tartisan is committed to ongoing engagement with First Nations and Indigenous communities as exploration planning advances. Work at Turtle Pond will follow the permit's terms, including advance notification and seasonal restrictions, as well as applicable early exploration standards and rehabilitation requirements.

Vancouver, Canada, Nov. 19, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Clearmind Medicine Inc. (Nasdaq: CMND) (“Clearmind” or the “Company”), a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company advancing non-hallucinogenic psychedelic-derived neuroplastogens for scalable treatment of neuropsychiatric, metabolic, and addiction disorders including Alcohol Use Disorder (“AUD”), today announced the publication of a Hong Kong patent application covering innovative psychedelic compounds targeting the treatment of Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (“PTSD”) and other mental health disorders.

The patent application is part of the Company's exclusive worldwide licensing agreement with Yissum Research Development Company of the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (“Yissum”). The compounds were invented by Professors Ahmed Masaewa, Rami Yaka, and Avi Priel of the Hebrew University. Under the licensing agreement, Clearmind holds exclusive global rights to develop, manufacture, and commercialize the novel compounds.

The Hong Kong patent publication expands Clearmind's global patent application portfolio for its proprietary PTSD-focused psychedelic compounds. Together with existing international filings, the application supports the Company's strategy to seek intellectual property protection for its novel therapeutic candidates across major global markets.

According to market research by Heimdall Insights, the global PTSD therapeutics market was valued at approximately $19 billion in 2025 and is projected to reach $24.8 billion by 2030, representing a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of approximately 5.5%. In addition, GlobalData projects that the PTSD pharmaceutical market across seven major markets is projected to grow from $1.2 billion in 2024 to $5.5 billion by 2034, at a CAGR of 16.1%,  reflecting anticipated demand for innovative treatment options.

About Clearmind Medicine Inc.

Clearmind is a clinical-stage neuroplastogens pharmaceutical biotech company focused on the discovery and development of non-hallucinogenic, second generation, neuroplastogen-derived therapeutics to solve widespread and underserved health problems, including alcohol use disorder. Its primary objective is to research and develop psychedelic-based compounds and attempt to commercialize them as regulated medicines, foods, or supplements.

The Company’s intellectual property portfolio currently consists of nineteen patent families, including 32 granted patents. The Company intends to seek additional patents for its compounds whenever warranted and will remain opportunistic regarding the acquisition of additional intellectual property to build its portfolio.

TEL AVIV, Israel, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Arbe Robotics Ltd. (NASDAQ: ARBE) (TASE: ARBE), a global leader in ultra-high-resolution radar solutions, today announced financial results for its third quarter ended September 30, 2026.

Recent Highlights

  • Level 3 automotive program win: One of the world's largest automotive groups selected Hirain's imaging radar, powered by Arbe's chipset, for a Level 3 passenger vehicle program across multiple brands in China. Series-production radar deliveries are scheduled to begin in the fourth quarter of 2027, putting Arbe on a defined path to automotive mass production.
  • Defense program advances to orders and deliveries: During the quarter, a leading global defense and homeland security system integrator selected Arbe for three civilian and defense projects under a framework agreement. Since the announcement, Arbe has received initial orders and delivered radar systems.
  • Alerion counter-drone radar launched: Arbe introduced Alerion, an ultra-high-resolution counter-drone radar, designed to detect small, low-flying threats, including hard-to-detect autonomous and fiber-optic drones. Alerion has been field-tested and is built to protect critical infrastructure and defense assets. As the threat continues to escalate, industry analysts expect significant growth in the global counter-UAS (Unmanned Aircraft Systems) market over the coming years.
  • Early defense momentum: Shortly after entering the defense market, Arbe is already seeing commercial engagement. Beyond the projects with the global system integrator described above, Arbe has initiated two additional integration projects addressing immediate customer needs and is in early-stage evaluations for more than eight projects.
  • Off road autonomy: During the quarter, Arbe's Tier 1, Sensrad, announced a collaboration with VirtuRail to integrate its radar system, based on Arbe's chipset, into automated tunnel construction vehicles operating in dust, smoke and darkness.
  • $15 million capital raise: Arbe closed a $15 million underwritten registered direct offering led by two leading US institutional investors, including AWM's Special Situations Funds, one of the major shareholders of Arbe. Together with a reduced quarterly cash burn, the proceeds strengthen Arbe's financial position and support scaling for its Level 3 automotive program, expansion into the defense segment and other growth initiatives.
  • New Chief Financial Officer: Arbe appointed Assaf Pereg, CPA, as Chief Financial Officer, effective August 30, 2026. He brings Arbe nearly 20 years of financial leadership experience in both US-listed public technology companies and start-ups.

Management Comments

Ram Machness, CEO of Arbe, commented, "The third quarter was a turning point for Arbe. Our Level 3 program win with one of the world's largest automotive groups validates years of development and testing and puts us on the path to automotive mass production. Furthermore, our $15 million capital raise, led by institutional investors, shows continued trust in our ongoing strategic plan."

"Building on our leading chipset technology, we are expanding our radar system portfolio beyond automotive, a key strategic step that opens new markets for us. Alongside Phoenix, our automotive radar system, this quarter we launched Alerion, our counter-drone radar. Alerion finds small, low-flying drones, including autonomous and fiber-optic drones that are hard for other sensors to detect. This strategy is already showing early results: a leading global system integrator selected us for three projects, and we have received orders and delivered systems, with more integration projects already underway. Defense and counter-drone programs have shorter sales cycles, and they are additive and complement our long-term automotive business. Our focus now is on turning customer interest into revenue."

Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results Highlights

Revenues for Q3 2026 were $0.8 million, compared to $0.3 million in Q3 2025.

Gross profit for Q3 2026 was approximately break-even, compared to a gross loss of $0.2 million in Q3 2025.

Operating expenses in Q3 2026 were $9.1 million, compared to $11.3 million in Q3 2025.

The lower expenses were primarily driven by lower share-based compensation expenses and lower labor costs paid this quarter, compared to Q3 2025. Operating loss in Q3 2026 was $9.1 million, compared to an $11.5 million loss in Q3 2025.

Net loss in Q3 2026 decreased to $9.0 million, compared to a net loss of $11.0 million in Q3 2025.

Adjusted EBITDA for Q3 2026, a non-GAAP measure that excludes expenses for non-cash share-based compensation and non-recurring items, improved to a loss of $8.0 million, compared with a loss of $9.2 million in Q3 2025.

Management believes that this non-GAAP measurement is important in evaluating our use of cash and in planning our cash requirements in the coming period.

Balance Sheet and Liquidity Highlights

As of September 30, 2026, Arbe had $48.0 million in cash, cash equivalents, long-term and short-term bank deposits. These include the $13.8 million net proceeds of the offering completed in September 2026.

As of September 30, 2026, Arbe had $46.3 million in shareholders' equity.

The Company remains in compliance with the financial covenants set forth in the convertible debentures and holds cash substantially above the minimum threshold.

Outlook

Arbe is updating its full-year 2026 outlook provided in February 2026.

Based on current market conditions and customer engagement visibility, the Company's outlook for 2026 is as follows:

  • Revenue in the range of $2.3 million to $3.0 million. The revised range reflects the timing of two integration projects, for which deliveries and related revenue recognition were originally expected in the fourth quarter of 2026 and have shifted to 2027.
  • Adjusted EBITDA for 2026 is projected to be a loss in the range of $34 million to $35 million. The revised range reflects lower expected revenue for 2026 and the Company's strategic investment in building a production line for radar systems and in building inventory to position the Company for potential order growth in the coming year.

This outlook reflects management's current expectations as of today and is subject to change based on market conditions, customer adoption timelines, and other factors.

Conference Call and Webcast Details

Arbe will host a conference call and webcast today, November 19, 2026, at 8:30 a.m. Eastern Time. Speakers will include Kobi Marenko, President and Co-Founder, Ram Machness, Chief Executive Officer, and Assaf Pereg, Chief Financial Officer.

Arbe (NASDAQ: ARBE), a global leader in ultra-high-resolution radar solutions, is redefining radar as a core sensing platform for next-generation mobility and advanced sensing applications. Arbe's complete radar technology stack, from proprietary chipsets to radar systems and AI algorithms that produce perception-ready data, delivers the detail and real-time processing that demanding sensing applications require. Company advances its internally developed drug discovery program targeting acute graft-versus-host disease (aGVHD) and AgPlenus' fungicide discovery programs targeting novel MoA against Septoria

REHOVOT, Israel, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Evogene Ltd. (Nasdaq: EVGN) (TASE: EVGN), a computational chemistry company leveraging proprietary AI-driven technologies to design and develop novel small molecules for the pharmaceutical and agricultural industries, today reported its financial results for the third quarter and first nine months of 2026, and provided an update on its business activities.

Ofer Haviv, Evogene's President and CEO, stated: "During the third quarter, we continued to advance our strategy of leveraging our proprietary AI-driven discovery platform, ChemPass AI™, to develop innovative small-molecule-based products with significant commercial potential. Alongside our collaborative discovery activities, we are advancing two internal development programs that represent an important component of our strategy to build a pipeline of proprietary assets fully owned and managed by Evogene.

The first one is our internal drug discovery program targeting acute graft-versus-host disease (aGVHD), a serious medical condition associated with significant unmet medical need. Within just several months, Using ChemPass AI™, we generated a series of novel, small-molecule candidates, that demonstrated biological potency, at nanomolar concentrations, as well as encouraging preliminary ADME and toxicology profiles. We are now focused on further optimizing these molecules, identifying the most promising candidates, and advancing the program toward IND-enabling studies. (For more information, please see our PR from 28, October 2026)

The second program, conducted through our subsidiary AgPlenus, focuses on discovering fungicides with new modes of action targeting Septoria tritici blotch, a major wheat disease for which resistance to existing fungicides is a growing challenge. Using ChemPass AI for Ag™, AgPlenus identified compounds that showed promising activity against fungicide-resistant Septoria strains. Selected compounds also reduced disease severity by up to 75%, compared to untreated controls, in plant tissue assays and demonstrating activity against additional fungal pathogens, indicating broader fungicidal potential. (For more information, please see our PR from 17, November 2026)

The progresses achieved across these initiatives demonstrates the ability of ChemPass AI™ and ChemPass AI for Ag™ to translate computational discovery into experimentally validated molecules exhibiting promising biological activity. More importantly, these programs reflect our strategic focus on converting technological capabilities into differentiated, proprietary product candidates offering meaningful commercial potential, ultimately creating long-term value for Evogene and its shareholders. "

Financial Results and Analysis

Cash Position

As of September 30, 2026, Evogene held consolidated cash, cash equivalents and short-term bank deposits of approximately $9.2 million. Consolidated cash usage during the third quarter of 2026 was approximately $2.4 million, including a Directors' and Officers' insurance payment of approximately $0.5 million, covering an 18-month period.

Revenues

Revenues for the nine months of 2026 totaled approximately $0.8 million, compared to approximately $3.2 million in the same period of 2025, representing a decrease of approximately $2.4 million. The decrease is mainly attributable to lower revenue recognized by Casterra, which in the first half of 2025 included significant seed sales of approximately $2.0 million. Revenues for the third quarter of 2026 were approximately $0.1 million compared to approximately $0.3 million in the third quarter of 2025, mainly due to the conclusion of the license and collaboration agreement with Bayer in May 2026.

Research and Development Expenses

Research and development expenses, net of non-refundable grants, for the nine months of 2026 were approximately $4.5 million, compared to approximately $4.6 million in the corresponding period of 2025, representing a decrease of approximately $0.1 million. For the third quarter of 2026, R&D expenses were approximately $1.5 million, an increase from $1.1 million in the same period of 2025. The increase was mainly attributable to the recognition of a non-refundable grant of approximately $0.2 million and an adjustment to liabilities in respect of government grants of approximately $0.1 million, both of which reduced R&D expenses in the third quarter of 2025, as well as the impact of fluctuations in the USD/NIS exchange rate, between the periods.

Sales and Marketing Expenses

Sales and marketing expenses for the nine months of 2026 were approximately $0.9 million, compared to approximately $1.1 million in the corresponding period of 2025. Sales and marketing expenses for the third quarter of 2026 were approximately $0.2 million, compared to approximately $0.4 million in the third quarter of 2025, primarily due to lower sales and marketing expenses at Casterra and AgPlenus.

General and Administrative Expenses

General and administrative expenses for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, decreased slightly to approximately $3.1 million, compared to approximately $3.2 million in the corresponding period of 2025. For the third quarter of 2026, general and administrative expenses were approximately $1.1 million, remaining relatively unchanged compared to the same period of 2025. The decrease in general and administrative expenses across Evogene and its subsidiaries was largely offset, mainly by transaction costs associated with the warrant inducement transaction and additional non-recurring legal expenses related to corporate governance and shareholders matters. These costs totaled approximately $0.4 million and $0.3 million during the nine-month and three-month periods ended September 30, 2026, respectively.

Financing Expenses (Income), Net

Financing expenses, net, for the nine months of 2026 were approximately $1.6 million, compared to financing income, net, of approximately $0.9 million in the corresponding period of 2025. This change was primarily related to the accounting treatment and revaluation of warrants, including warrants issued in the August 2024 financing and the February 2026 warrant inducement transaction. As part of the February 2026 warrant inducement transaction, the Company recorded financing expenses of approximately $3.8 million during the first nine months of 2026. In addition, the Company recorded financing income of approximately $2.3 million related to the revaluation of warrants liability as of September 30, 2026. For the third quarter of 2026, financing income, net, was approximately $176 thousand, compared to approximately $79 thousand in the corresponding period of 2025, with no material change between the periods.

Loss from Discontinued Operations

Loss from discontinued operations, net, for the nine months of 2026 was approximately $0.5 million, compared to an income from discontinued operations, net, of approximately $4.0 million in the corresponding period of 2025. For the third quarter of 2026, the loss from discontinued operations was approximately $0.06 million, compared to income of approximately $7.6 million in the third quarter of the previous year. These amounts primarily reflect the financial results of Lavie Bio's and Biomica's operations, as well as expenses related to the development and maintenance of MicroBoost AI for Ag, which are presented as a single-line item in the consolidated statements of profit and loss. Following the sale of the majority of Lavie Bio's assets, as well as Evogene's MicroBoost AI for Ag, to ICL in July 2025 and the licensing agreement with Lishan in February 2026, Lavie Bio's and Biomica's operating expense levels have decreased significantly. Biomica's operations were classified as discontinued operations beginning in the second quarter of 2026, and accordingly, the 2025 comparative figures have been reclassified to conform to the current period presentation. Lavie Bio's operations, as well as expenses related to the development and maintenance of MicroBoost AI for Ag, had already been classified as discontinued operations in 2025.

Net loss for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, was approximately $10.5 million, compared to approximately $2.5 million in the corresponding period of 2025. The $8.0 million increase in net loss was primarily attributable to lower revenues, higher financing expenses, and income recognized in connection with the ICL transaction during the corresponding period of 2025. For the third quarter of 2026, net loss was approximately $2.9 million, compared to net income of approximately $5.2 million in the same period of 2025. The change was primarily attributable to income recognized in connection with the ICL transaction during the third quarter of 2025, as discussed above.

About Evogene Ltd.

Evogene Ltd. (NASDAQ: EVGN) (TASE: EVGN) is a pioneering company in computational chemistry, specializing in the generative design of small molecules for drug development and ag chemical products. At the core of its technology is ChemPass AITM, a proprietary generative AI designed to explore vast chemical space and generate novel, highly potent small molecules optimized across multiple critical parameters. Built on this powerful technological foundation, and through strategic partnerships alongside internal product development, Evogene is focused on creating breakthrough products for the pharmaceutical and agricultural industries, driven by the integration of scientific innovation with real-world industry needs.

For more information, please visit www.evogene.com. 

About AgPlenus Ltd. 

AgPlenus, a subsidiary of Evogene Ltd., is an AI-driven crop protection discovery company focused on developing effective and sustainable solutions to address the growing challenge of pesticide resistance. The company leverages ChemPass AI for Ag™, a technology platform licensed from Evogene, integrating predictive biology, artificial intelligence, and computational chemistry to discover novel crop-protection molecules. Through its target-based discovery approach, AgPlenus aims to improve discovery efficiency, reduce development risks, and advance differentiated crop-protection solutions with the potential to address unmet agricultural needs. 

For more information, please visit www.agplenus.com

Integration will bring three Canadian-hosted AI models to Railtown's Conductr platform and AI Partner Marketplace, combining Canadian AI inference with Railtown's agent development, knowledge infrastructure and deployment technologies.

Vancouver, British Columbia--(Newsfile Corp. - November 19, 2026) - Railtown AI Technologies Inc. (CSE: RAIL) (OTCQB: RLAIF) ("Railtown" or the "Company") is pleased to announce a Technology Integration Partnership with Radium, a frontier model alternative with drop-in LLM APIs to replace OpenAI and Anthropic. Radium's models, Hal, Clarke and Tycho, are available with hosting in Canada.

Under the partnership, Railtown and Radium are working to integrate three of Radium's AI models directly into Railtown's Conductr platform, making them accessible to Railtown customers and participating technology partners within the AI Partner Marketplace.

The integration is intended to provide developers and organizations with additional model choices while supporting growing demand for AI solutions that prioritize Canadian data residency, security and operational control.

By combining Radium's Canadian-hosted AI models with Railtown's Conductr, Railengine and Railtracks technologies, the companies aim to provide a comprehensive technology foundation for building, deploying and managing intelligent AI applications and agents.

Addressing the Growing Demand for Sovereign AI

As artificial intelligence adoption accelerates across Canadian businesses and institutions, data sovereignty is becoming an increasingly important consideration in technology procurement and deployment decisions.

Organizations operating in industries such as financial services, healthcare, government and professional services must consider where sensitive information is stored, processed and accessed when evaluating AI solutions.

While many organizations are eager to adopt AI-powered applications, concerns surrounding data residency, privacy, security and reliance on foreign-hosted infrastructure can create barriers to implementation.

The Railtown and Radium partnership is designed to help address these requirements by combining Canadian-hosted AI model inference with the development, knowledge management, deployment and observability capabilities available through Railtown's technology ecosystem.

Radium's Canadian hosting options provide an important component of this approach, while Railtown's technology enables developers and organizations to build and operate applications around those models.

Together, the companies intend to provide customers with greater flexibility in designing AI solutions that align with their data-residency and operational requirements.

Three Radium AI Models to Be Integrated into Conductr

The integration will introduce three Radium models into Railtown's Conductr platform, providing developers with options for selecting AI models based on application requirements, performance characteristics and workload complexity.

Hal - Advanced Reasoning and Agent Workflows

Designed for complex reasoning, coding, tool execution and sophisticated multi-step agent workflows.

Clarke - Enterprise Knowledge and Conversational AI

Designed for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), knowledge-based applications, conversational AI and enterprise information retrieval.

Tycho - High-Efficiency AI Processing

Designed for high-volume workloads, including document classification, information extraction and other applications where processing efficiency is important.

Through Conductr, customers will be able to select Radium models as part of their agent development and deployment workflows, subject to completion of the integration.

This approach supports Railtown's broader strategy of providing developers with access to multiple AI models and infrastructure providers through a unified technology platform.

Combining Canadian-Hosted AI Models with Railtown's Technology Ecosystem

Railtown's technology platform is designed to support the lifecycle of intelligent applications and AI agents. Refer to News Release dated October 15th, 2026, for description of commercialization.

Its core technologies include:

  • Conductr: Railtown's agentic AI orchestration, deployment and observability platform, providing developers and organizations with capabilities to deploy, manage, monitor and evaluate AI agents.
  • Railengine: Railtown's knowledge and data infrastructure, enabling AI applications and agents to access relevant enterprise information and persistent knowledge bases.
  • Railtracks: Railtown's open-source Agent Development Kit, providing developers with frameworks for creating specialized AI agents and intelligent workflows.

The addition of Radium's Canadian-hosted models is intended to complement these capabilities by providing model inference options for organizations seeking Canadian data residency.

For customers requiring a sovereign AI architecture, the combined technologies can support solutions in which model inference, enterprise knowledge and agent workloads are configured to operate within approved Canadian infrastructure environments.

The resulting architecture is intended to give customers greater control over their AI technology choices while simplifying the development and management of production AI applications.

Extending Sovereign AI Capabilities Through Canadian Data Centre Partnerships

Beyond providing access to Canadian-hosted AI models, Railtown is pursuing a broader strategy of working with Canadian cloud and data centre infrastructure providers to support sovereign AI deployments.

Through these relationships, Railtown aims to combine its Conductr, Railengine and Railtracks technologies with Canadian-hosted computing infrastructure, enabling organizations to build, deploy and manage intelligent applications while maintaining greater control over where their enterprise data, knowledge bases and AI workloads reside.

The integration of Radium's Canadian-hosted models represents an important complementary component of this strategy.

While Radium provides Canadian-based AI model inference, Railtown's technology ecosystem provides the software infrastructure required to connect enterprise knowledge, develop specialized AI agents, orchestrate intelligent workflows and monitor their execution.

By bringing these capabilities together with Canadian data centre infrastructure, Railtown intends to support more comprehensive sovereign AI architectures in which model inference, enterprise knowledge and agent execution can be configured to operate within Canadian hosting environments.

This approach is particularly relevant for Canadian small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), government organizations and businesses operating in regulated industries that want to adopt artificial intelligence while addressing data residency, privacy and security requirements.

Railtown believes that combining Canadian-hosted AI models, Canadian infrastructure providers and its proprietary software technologies will help reduce the complexity of deploying sovereign AI solutions and provide Canadian organizations with a more accessible path to adopting production-ready agentic applications.

Importantly, this strategy also provides Railtown with opportunities to expand its commercial relationships with infrastructure providers, technology integration partners and customers seeking Canadian-hosted AI solutions.

Management Commentary

Cory Brandolini, Chief Executive Officer of Railtown AI, commented:

"One of the most important developments we are seeing in the Canadian AI market is the growing demand for sovereign AI solutions. Canadian organizations increasingly want the benefits of artificial intelligence, but they also want greater control over where their data resides, where their applications operate and how their AI infrastructure is managed.

"We have been working closely with the Radium team over the last several quarters, testing their models and APIs, and our development team has been extremely impressed with both the quality of their technology and the capabilities of their models. Radium has built an impressive AI offering, and we believe their Canadian-hosted models are a natural complement to Railtown's technology ecosystem.

"What makes this partnership particularly compelling is the combination of our respective technologies. Radium provides the AI models and Canadian hosting capabilities, while Railtown provides the tools and infrastructure developers need to build, connect, deploy and observe intelligent applications. Together, we believe we can help Canadian businesses move beyond experimenting with AI toward implementing practical, production-ready solutions that address their operational and data-residency requirements.

"Our strategy extends beyond integrating AI models. We are actively building relationships with Canadian data centre and cloud infrastructure providers to create a broader ecosystem for sovereign AI deployment. When you combine Canadian-hosted models from Radium with Railtown's agent development, knowledge infrastructure, deployment and observability technologies, and the ability to run critical workloads within Canadian data centres, we believe you have the foundation for a compelling end-to-end sovereign AI solution. This is particularly important for Canadian SMEs that want to adopt AI but may not have the internal technical resources to assemble and manage these technologies themselves.

"We also see an important commercial opportunity through our AI Partner Marketplace. By making Radium's models available to our growing network of technology partners, we can provide those companies with additional tools to develop and deliver sovereign AI solutions to their own customers. We believe this creates opportunities for both companies while strengthening Railtown's position within Canada's emerging sovereign AI ecosystem."

Expanding Opportunities Through the AI Partner Marketplace

The Radium integration is also expected to benefit Railtown's AI Partner Marketplace, a commercial ecosystem designed to connect AI technology providers with prospective customers and support the commercialization of AI applications and services.

Through the Marketplace, participating technology partners will have the opportunity to incorporate Radium's models into AI solutions developed using Railtown's technology infrastructure.

This will provide partners with additional options when serving customers that prioritize Canadian data residency or require greater flexibility in selecting AI model providers.

Railtown believes that expanding the range of available AI technologies within its ecosystem will enhance the value of the Marketplace to participating companies and create additional opportunities for technology integration, customer acquisition and recurring platform revenue.

The partnership also supports Railtown's broader strategy of bringing together complementary AI technology providers through Conductr and its AI Partner Marketplace.

Radium Management Commentary

Adam Hendin, Cofounder / CEO of Radium, commented:

"Hal, Clarke and Tycho are built to stand alongside the frontier models, and Canadian companies should be able to run them at home. Railtown gives teams building agents on Conductr a direct way to do that."

About Radium

Radium is a frontier model alternative with drop-in LLM APIs to replace OpenAI and Anthropic. Its models, Hal, Clarke and Tycho, are served from Radium's own infrastructure, including in Canada. Radium is headquartered in San Francisco, with a second headquarters in Canada.

For more information, visit https://radium.cloud.

Railtown AI Technologies Inc. is an AI technology company developing tools and infrastructure that enable developers and organizations to build, deploy, manage and observe AI-powered applications and agents.

Its technology includes Conductr, an agentic AI orchestration, deployment and observability platform; Railengine, its knowledge and data infrastructure; and Railtracks, its open-source Agent Development Kit.

Railtown is focused on simplifying the development and operation of agentic applications while supporting organizations seeking flexible, secure and scalable AI solutions.
